speaker: Doctor
text: The rash suggests a possible hypersensitivity reaction, but the persistent fever and flank pain raise concern for a kidney infection or interstitial nephritis. Do you have any pain or burning when you urinate, and have you noticed any changes in your urine frequency or color? I would also like to know if you have experienced any nausea or vomiting alongside these symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of antibiotic use, rash, and current symptoms of fever and flank pain without typical urinary tract symptoms, I suspect Acute Interstitial Nephritis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_with_microscopy. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Creatinine.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of eosinophils in the urine alongside acute kidney injury and a history of antibiotic-induced rash strongly supports Acute Interstitial Nephritis rather than pyelonephritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
